sources.title: Van Ravensteijn et al. (2017), Fuel-Mediated Transient Clustering of Colloidal Building Blocks
sources.access_depth: Primary full-text university repository PDF, selected passages
sources.inspected: Scheme 1 and Figs. 1–3; fuel-induced change in surface interactions drives assembly; depletion restores repulsion.

sources.title: Sharma, Sarkar and Walther (2023), Transient Co-Assemblies of Micron-Scale Colloids Regulated by ATP-Fueled Reaction Networks
sources.access_depth: Primary publisher-hosted full accepted manuscript, selected passages
sources.inspected: Figs. 2, 4 and 5; no-fuel control, variable fuel dose and pathway control; Fig. 4 fluorescence lifetime increases about 6 to 10 h for the tested 40 to 60 µM doses. RSC HTML returned HTTP 403; corresponding indexed PMC record is https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10631234/.

sources.title: Sharma (2023), Designing Chemical Reaction Networks for Self-Assembly of Colloids
sources.access_depth: University repository full dissertation PDF, selected Chapter 5 and supplements
sources.inspected: Fig. 5-8: static versus transient soluble complexation. Static arm omits BsaI, with fuel-induced ligation still present.

sources.title: Boekhoven et al. (2015), Transient assembly of active materials fueled by a chemical reaction
sources.access_depth: Primary article abstract and metadata only
sources.inspected: DOI 10.1126/science.aac6103. Abstract reports fuel-dependent lifetime, stiffness and self-regeneration. Publisher article through authors' publication list returned HTTP 403.

sources.title: Koper et al. (2013), Dissipative Self-Assembly: A Novel Self-Healing Mechanism for Functional Materials
sources.access_depth: Primary full conference paper PDF, selected passages
sources.inspected: Fig. 3b–d and discussion compare monomer concentration and storage modulus with relative recovery after mechanical perturbation. Recovery is strongest in the more active early phase of the batch.

sources.title: Kriebisch et al. (2023), Kinetic Traps in Chemically Fueled Self-Assembly and How to Overcome Them
sources.access_depth: Primary full text from publisher PDF copy in university repository, selected passages
sources.inspected: Scheme 1, Fig. 1: chemical deactivation may leave the assembly kinetically trapped; activated monomers can be regenerated within it.

sources.title: Fullerton and Jack (2016), Optimising self-assembly through time-dependent interactions
sources.access_depth: Primary arXiv full HTML, selected passages
sources.inspected: Sections II–IV and Fig. 5. Fixed switch protocol ε(t)=ε1 before t_step, ε2 after; constant diagonal ε1=ε2; terminal N_Q and N_G for the tested arms.

sources.title: Trubiano and Hagan (2022), Optimization of Non-Equilibrium Self-Assembly Protocols Using Markov State Models
sources.access_depth: Primary arXiv full HTML and PDF, selected theory and results
sources.inspected: Eq. (2) maximizes terminal P_B^N penalized by squared finite differences of design variables; Eq. (7) is terminal payoff conditioned on intermediate state; Fig. 7 compares fixed and time-varying. PMC direct open presented a CAPTCHA.

sources.title: Klotsa and Jack (2013), Controlling crystal self-assembly using a real-time feedback scheme
sources.access_depth: Primary arXiv full HTML, selected methods and results
sources.inspected: Eq. (4), Fig. 2: sampled reversibility of bonds controls externally updated bond strength; compared with no-feedback runs.

sources.title: Whitelam and Schmit (2022), Low-dissipation self-assembly protocols of active sticky particles
sources.access_depth: Primary full manuscript PDF, selected methods and results
sources.inspected: Eqs. (10)–(13) and Figs. 5–7: final fraction of solid-like particles with a trajectory entropy cost; time-driven protocols vary propulsion and attraction. PMC direct open presented a CAPTCHA.

sources.title: Synthetic paracrine signaling of colloids drives self-assembly limit cycles (2026)
sources.access_depth: Primary arXiv preprint full HTML, selected introduction and model
sources.inspected: Eq. (2) evolves bond strengths via exponential decay and a sum of sign-coded nearby sources. The physical sketch invokes fuel; simulation evolves effective signals and does not close a finite fuel inventory.

sources.title: Extended Onsager’s variational principle for nonlinear chemical reaction kinetics in active matter (2026)
sources.access_depth: Primary arXiv preprint full HTML, selected §III.1
sources.inspected: Eqs. (43)–(46), (50)–(53): parallel passive and fuel-conversion channels in a closed ideal reactor, with mass-action dynamics and a conservation law. No first-failure optimization.

sources.title: Goyal et al. (2025), On repairable systems with time redundancy and operational constraints
sources.access_depth: Primary full-text publisher PDF in university repository, selected §4
sources.inspected: Proposition 4.1 and Box I: Laplace transform of first-failure time with a gross cap on repairs.

sources.title: Vora et al., Solving Truly Massive Budgeted Monotonic POMDPs with Oracle-Guided Meta-Reinforcement Learning
sources.access_depth: Primary arXiv preprint full HTML, selected introduction, framework and results
sources.inspected: Shared finite intervention budget; weak coupling across components; value concavity and explicit optimization. No assembly dynamics or detailed-balance reverses.

sources.title: Zhang and Isaacson, Detailed Balance for Particle Models of Reversible Reactions in Bounded Domains
sources.access_depth: Primary arXiv full HTML, selected detailed-balance construction building on prior workspace audit
sources.inspected: Sec. III and Theorem III.1; probability fluxes on paired reversible reaction kernels at equilibrium.

sources.title: Mean-field models for the chemical fueling of transient soft matter states
sources.access_depth: Primary arXiv full HTML, selected §II and discussion
sources.inspected: Eqs. (2), (6)–(8): finite initial concentration of fuel creates a transient interaction partner, which shifts a bistable mechanical landscape. Quasistatic and Smoluchowski treatments; no shared repair channel.

sources.title: England (2015), Dissipative adaptation in driven self-assembly
sources.access_depth: Original perspective full PDF, selected argument and scope
sources.inspected: External driving and work-conditioned transition probabilities; limits of inference from dissipation alone. No finite-reserve reliability comparison.

sources.title: A material system with integrated fault diagnosis and feedback controlled self-healing
sources.access_depth: Publisher index excerpt only; direct full open timed out
sources.inspected: Nearby use of external energy and structural fault diagnosis. No full-text novelty inference drawn.

sources.title: Ragazzon and Prins (2018), Energy consumption in chemical fuel-driven self-assembly
sources.access_depth: Perspective postprint indexed excerpts used for terminology and source finding
sources.inspected: Distinguishes supplying fuel to an implementation from coupling assembled states to energy transduction.

sources.title: Boekhoven et al. (2010), Dissipative Self-Assembly of a Molecular Gelator by Using a Chemical Fuel
sources.access_depth: Primary publisher metadata and graphical abstract
sources.inspected: Early fuel-driven gelation followed by relaxation after depletion. Fig. 3 recovery details taken from the separate full 2013 report.

sources.title: Programmable supramolecular chirality in non-equilibrium systems affording a multistate chiroptical switch
sources.access_depth: Publisher index and indexed PMC excerpt; direct publisher open failed via inaccessible identity-provider redirect
sources.inspected: Search lead on pathway-dependent kinetic trapping only.

sources.title: Chemically fueled materials with a self-immolative mechanism: transient materials with a fast on/off response
sources.access_depth: Publisher PDF indexed excerpt; full HTML 403
sources.inspected: Search lead on finite fuel and autonomous decay only.

sources.title: Kar et al. (2025 issue, 2024 online), Transient transition from Stable to Dissipative Assemblies in Response to the Spatiotemporal Availability of a Chemical Fuel
sources.access_depth: Primary publisher full HTML and university repository copy of full publisher PDF, selected passages and figures
sources.inspected: Figs. 1–3: thermal assemblies coexist with transients produced by local fuel pulses and diffusion. Fixed dose and different template levels; no shared repair reserve or failure-time optimum.

sources.title: Van der Helm, de Beun and Eelkema (2021), On the use of catalysis to bias reaction pathways in out-of-equilibrium systems
sources.access_depth: Primary full publisher PDF with TU Delft cover, selected schemes and results
sources.inspected: Scheme 1 and Figs. 1–2: batch ODEs with catalytic and uncatalyzed routes and a scan of product half-lives; Scheme 2 and Fig. 6: state-dependent negative feedback versus fixed catalyst in open flow.

sources.title: Transiently amplified fluctuations assemble dissipative materials (2026)
sources.access_depth: Primary full-text PMC HTML, selected results and methods
sources.inspected: Fig. 1 and Eqs. (25)–(30), (47): external reservoirs drive transient assembly amplification at fixed microscopic rate constants. No closed matched budget or first-failure test.

sources.title: Grötsch et al. (2019), Pathway Dependence in the Fuel-Driven Dissipative Self-Assembly of Nanoparticles
sources.access_depth: Primary publisher abstract; authors' thesis copy surfaced as a lead
sources.inspected: Same total quantity of fuel added as one dose or multiple doses yields different morphologies and trapping behavior. Source lead only.

scope_limit: Targeted search without a systematic claim of completeness. Selected full-text passages were read, and abstract/index-only access is identified. No external contact was made.
